facts.text: My arm is weak.
It's my right arm.
It came on gradually, more than 5 years ago.
The first thing I noticed was that I couldn't keep a grip on things I was holding.
Gradually it became hard to do fine things like buttoning my clothes, writing, combing my hair and using cutlery.
Over the same years the muscles of my right hand have been getting thinner.
My hands shake.
Both hands.
It started in my right hand over the same period as the weakness; my left hand started shaking about 2 years after the right-hand problems began.
My left hand isn't weak.
Everything got worse over the first 3 years, but it has stayed the same since then.
I don't have neck pain.
I haven't had any changes in feeling, no numbness or tingling.
I haven't had any problems with my body's automatic functions.
I don't have any problems with my bladder.
I don't have any problems with my bowels.
I haven't had any injuries.
I've never had surgery.
I don't take any medications.
I haven't had any vaccinations.
I haven't been exposed to any toxins.
I'm a university student, and I work part-time.
Nobody in my family has had a neurological disease.
I'm Nepalese.

findings.name: motor examination
findings.result: Bulk: atrophy of the right hand, most prominently in the first dorsal interosseous, with sparing of the brachioradialis. Tone: reduced around the right elbow and wrist. Strength (MRC): right interossei 2/5, wrist flexion and extension 3/5, elbow flexion and extension 4/5; left upper-limb strength normal.

findings.name: involuntary movements
findings.result: Minipolymyoclonus in the fingers bilaterally, more pronounced on the right.

findings.name: deep tendon reflexes
findings.result: Symmetrical and normal except for a brisk right supinator response.

findings.name: autoimmune serology
findings.result: ANA, anti-dsDNA and ANCA within normal limits.

findings.name: nerve conduction studies
findings.result: Motor axonal neuropathy with reduced compound motor action potentials in the right median and ulnar nerves; normal on the left.

findings.name: needle EMG
findings.result: Neurogenic discharges with fibrillations and fasciculations in bilateral first dorsal interossei and the right biceps and triceps.

findings.name: cervical spine MRI
findings.result: Flexion T1-weighted contrast and neutral T2-weighted sequences: no dural enhancement, no anterior displacement of the posterior dural sac, no cord atrophy or signal abnormality.

aliases: juvenile muscular atrophy of the distal upper extremity
juvenile asymmetric segmental spinal muscular atrophy
gold.reasoning: 1. Alternative motor-neuron and neuropathic syndromes ruled out by history, exam, and electrophysiology — “With medical history, examination, and NCT/EMG features, spinal muscular atrophy, ALS, post-polio syndrome, multifocal motor neuropathy, anterior interosseous or deep ulnar neuropathy, and toxic neuropathy were ruled out.” 2. Structural spinal cord lesions excluded by imaging — “Cervical MRI helped to rule out syringomyelia, traumatic myelopathy, spinal tumors, and other spinal diseases.”

source_issues: The flexion MRI shows none of the typical findings (no anterior displacement of the posterior dural sac), as the selection note says.
notes: Index visit: the outpatient presentation after more than 5 years of insidious right upper-limb weakness (s001-s023; the earlier MRI is a timed finding).
The overall course (worse over 3 years, static since) applies to all symptoms and is a standalone fact; the tremor's sides and staggered onset are children of one tremor fact.
Sensation and gait are reported twice (s011, s017) and are one finding each citing both sentences.
s018 lists nine groups of normal laboratory tests; each orderable test or panel is its own record with the same result.
Harmonisation: the single 'vital signs' record was split into one record per standard parameter with the source's word; no oxygen saturation, which the source does not mention.
